findings.description: The environment attestation `pin_tree_identical_to_head` is computed with `git diff --quiet "$PIN" HEAD -- evals/harness evals/suites evals/fixtures ...`, which compares two commits. Everything the script then executes is read from the working tree: `bash evals/harness/run-ablation.sh` at line 69, `python3 -I evals/analysis/c132/record_lite.py` at line 64, and the grader / ablation-row scripts record_lite.py invokes. Uncommitted edits to evals/harness, the suite tasks or the fixtures are invisible to the check, so the report records that the pipeline tree is byte-identical to the pin while modified code produced the grades. The compared path set also excludes evals/analysis/c132 itself, so the field name overstates what was verified even between commits.
findings.failure_mode: A reproduction run on a clone with local modifications emits environment.json and report.md asserting pin-identical pipeline code, yet grades, rows and the DEC-0812 live sample were produced by different harness/grader scripts; the FR-10 attestation is unfalsifiable from the report alone.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare the working tree with the pin instead of HEAD (`git diff --quiet "$PIN" -- <paths>`), additionally require `git status --porcelain -- <paths>` to be empty (fail closed unless --no-env-check), record `git describe --always --dirty` in environment.json, and either add evals/analysis/c132 to the compared paths or rename the field to state it covers harness/suites/fixtures only.

findings.description: `--no-env-check` turns the image-digest and pin-tree failures into recorded facts but does not gate what follows: record_lite.py still launches grader containers from the mutable tag `loa-ablation:258`, and `--live-sample` still runs `evals/harness/run-ablation.sh` with the operator's model credentials and up to `--max-usd` (default 110) against an image whose digest did not match the registration and a harness that may differ from the pin. The runner's DEC-0435 gate is satisfied by passing the tracked historical log `self-check-c132.txt` rather than a fresh self-check, so in that configuration nothing verifies the image at run time, and the rerun grades are appended to the report as a pin-level sample.
findings.failure_mode: Credentials and budget are spent executing unverified container code; the live-sample table lands in the report with the same framing as a verified rerun, so a reader cannot tell the apparatus check was meaningless.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse `--live-sample` (exit 2) when envcheck is off or when image_matches/pin_same are false; verify the digest recorded inside self-check-c132.txt equals `$img` before passing it, or let run-ablation.sh perform a fresh self-check; mark the live table in the report with the environment.json verdicts.

findings.description: write_sample refuses to run when OUT/packets already holds files, but overwrites OUT/key.json unconditionally and item ids restart at D0001 for every sample. run-judge-defects.sh copies the packets away into chunk directories, so a second `sample` with a different seed or --per-arm after the packets directory is cleared replaces the key silently. `aggregate` validates labels only by item-id membership in key["items"] (validate(), load_labels()), so labels produced by judge sessions over the earlier packets are accepted against the new key and attributed to different (cell, defect) pairs.
findings.failure_mode: Silently wrong defect-level shares and corrected recall in result.json/result.md with no error, undermining the blind-judge integrity the provenance scan is built to protect.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse when OUT/key.json already exists (or require --force), embed a sample identifier (e.g. the first 12 hex of sha256(key.json without that field)) in every packet header and in labels.json, and have aggregate reject labels whose sample identifier differs from the key's.

findings.description: sha256_file is the integrity primitive behind sandbox-manifest.json, the pr/-vs-fixture comparison and the reconstruct sha-check, yet it memoises digests by (st_dev, st_ino, st_size, st_mtime_ns) taken with follow_symlinks=False while the content is read through open(path), which follows symlinks. A file rewritten in place within one process with preserved size and mtime (shutil.copy2, cp -p, rsync -t onto an existing inode) or a symlink whose target changes returns the cached digest for bytes that were never hashed.
findings.failure_mode: A reconstruction or --check comparison reports a file identical to its manifest entry although the bytes differ, so a differing artefact can be certified as reproduced.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not cache on verification paths (hash always when comparing), or key the cache on os.path.realpath(path) plus a stat taken with follow_symlinks=True including st_ctime_ns; keep the cache for the build-side fixture map only.

findings.cross_file_justification: final.sh is the committed driver that produced the tracked final/placebo/judge-sample reads which the diff's reproduce.sh (REGISTRATION-15 hardcoded at line 28) and reads.py (new co_reads and review_derived_labels in final_reads) target for byte-for-byte reproduction; the registration final.sh actually ran under is taken from an untracked cache file executed as shell, so the tracked artefacts' provenance depends on state outside the repository.
findings.description: `source ~/.cache/loa/cycle-132/registration.txt` executes an unversioned file as shell code to obtain REG_SHA, PIN and REG, and `cd /home/merlin/Documents/thj/code/loa` (line 8; same at run-judge-defects.sh line 5) binds the committed script to one developer's home directory. Any write to that cache file by another local process, a backup restore or a stray redirect runs arbitrary commands with the operator's privileges and model credentials, and the registration used for the tracked reads is whatever that file said rather than a tracked value.
findings.failure_mode: Arbitrary command execution from a cache file during the reads/judge runs; tracked read artefacts whose registration cannot be established from the repository; a developer username and local path published in committed scripts.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse the three values with a whitelist instead of sourcing (e.g. `REG=$(grep -E '^REG=' "$f" | cut -d= -f2-)`) or pass them as arguments; derive the repo root from `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` as reproduce.sh does; apply the same to run-judge-defects.sh.
